0.note: The superscription to this psalm identifies it as a **maskil**. Since the meaning of this word is not certain, you may wish to represent it in its Hebrew form and spell it the way it sounds in your language. See the discussion of that term in the Introduction to Psalms.

1.q: ק֭וֹלִ⁠י אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֶזְעָ֑ק ק֝וֹלִ֗⁠י אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֶתְחַנָּֽן
1.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Another approach would be to connect the phrases with a word that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in the Psalms, and follow that approach here and throughout this psalm. Alternate translation: [I earnestly cry out to Yahweh for favor]
David is using **My voice** to represent his prayer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [My prayer to Yahweh]

2.note: David is speaking of his lament as if it were a liquid that he **pours out** before Yahweh. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I express my lament to his face]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **lament**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what I lament]

Here, **to his face** represents being in the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in his presence]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **distress**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what distresses me]

3.note: David is using the word **spirit** to represent his whole self. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [When I grow faint]

The word **you** is repeated for emphasis. David is emphasizing that Yahweh is the one who truly knows his path. If your language does not use repetition for emphasis, you could express this in another way. Alternate translation: [then you alone know]

David is speaking of how he lives and what he does as if that were a **path** that he was walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my situation]

David is speaking of his enemies’ schemes as if they were a **trap** that **they** had **hidden** for him to fall into. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they have secretly planned to harm me]

David is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense to refer to his enemies without specifying who they are. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [others have hidden] or [people have hidden]

4.note: This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please look right and see]

Looking to the right was a symbolic action by which a person looked for his defender, since the right side was the position where a protector would stand. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Look for my defender]

David is using the word **soul** to represent his whole self. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me]

5.note: David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a **shelter** that could protect him from danger. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my protection]

David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a **portion** of inherited land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all that matters to me]

The expression **the land of the living** was a common expression meaning “among those who are alive on earth.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [during my life on earth]

David is using the adjective **living** as a noun to mean people who are alive. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [those who are alive]

6.note: The word **for** indicates that what follows is the reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because I am very low]

David is speaking of his distress as if he were physically in a **low** position. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am very weak]

The word **for** indicates that what follows is the reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [since they are stronger than I]

7.note: David is speaking of his trouble as if it were a **prison** from which he needs to be brought out. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Free me from my troubles]

David is using the word **soul** to represent his whole self. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me]

Here, **to** marks **praise your name** as the purpose for which David asks Yahweh to bring him out of trouble. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that I may praise your name]

David is using the term **name** to represent who Yahweh is and his reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you]

David is using the adjective **righteous** as a noun to mean righteous people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [Righteous people]

The word **because** indicates that what follows is the reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [for you will fulfill for me]

The implication is that Yahweh will fulfill David’s request or his promise. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [you will fulfill your promise to me] or [you will answer my prayer]
